discovery: The optical lattice clock: magic-wavelength trapping of neutral atoms enabling optical frequency standards at the 10^-18 level

nominees.name: Hidetoshi Katori
nominees.affiliation: University of Tokyo and RIKEN, Japan

nominees.name: Jun Ye
nominees.affiliation: JILA, NIST and University of Colorado Boulder, USA

motivation: Katori conceived the optical lattice clock (2001-2005): confining many neutral atoms in a light-shift-free 'magic wavelength' lattice so that Doppler and recoil shifts vanish while retaining the statistical power of large ensembles. This broke the prevailing view that only single trapped ions could reach ultimate accuracy. Jun Ye, combining frequency-comb technology, ultrastable lasers and many-body control of strontium lattices, drove these clocks to systematic uncertainties and instabilities near 10^-18 and below, resolving gravitational redshift across a millimetre-scale sample. Together their work made optical clocks a thousandfold better than caesium standards, motivating redefinition of the SI second, enabling relativistic geodesy, and providing new tests of fundamental constants and dark-matter searches. This is precision measurement transformed by quantum control, the direct heir of the 2005 frequency-comb prize, and a discovery with enduring impact across physics and technology.
